Hands-on experience building production-grade dbt projects with testing, documentation, and version control workflows. Strong proficiency in Python for analytics tasks (data checks, automation, utilities). Strong stakeholder management and communication skills — able to translate business logic into durable, scalable data models. Familiarity with ELT concepts, CI/CD for analytics code, data cataloging, and basic cost/performance tuning. Self-starter with a hands-on, problem-solving mindset, comfortable balancing autonomy and collaboration in a fast-moving environment. title: Full Stack Engineer (m/f/d)
description: TL;DR Join GlassDollar and help build the system some of Europe's largest companies use to find, test, and adopt startup technology. We're looking for an engineer who wants considerably more responsibility than "implement what's in the ticket". You'll take an ambiguous problem, shape it together with product, make the important technical decisions, ship it, and stay close enough to see whether it worked. We expect you to have opinions. We also expect you to be good enough to change them. The problem we're solving Large organisations are remarkably good at accumulating problems. A company with 100,000 employees can have thousands of operational challenges across its business units. Somewhere outside that organisation, a startup has probably already built part of the solution. Getting those two things to meet still happens through spreadsheets, long email threads, and meetings whose primary output is another meeting. GlassDollar OS is the operating system for venture clienting: problem → startup discovery → evaluation → PoC → adoption, in one repeatable workflow. Our customers are some of Europe's largest organisations, so the software has to move quickly and behave like something an enterprise can depend on. That tension creates the interesting engineering problems. What we're looking for You can take a problem further than the ticket. Work often starts with something incomplete, like "customers need a better way to manage X". You'll shape the problem with product, challenge assumptions, and decide what belongs in this iteration. Strong opinions about what we build, not only how, are expected here. You care about product. You want to know who you're building for, why the problem matters, and what success looks like. That context should shape your technical decisions. You have technical judgement. There is rarely one correct architecture. You know when the boring solution beats the ambitious one, when an abstraction helps and when it hides the problem, and when a small feature is about to create six months of technical debt. We expect you to reason about API boundaries, data models, permissions, performance, failure modes, testing, observability, and rollout, and to raise concerns with a clear argument attached. You make the system better, not just the feature. You fix the spreading pattern rather than the single instance, make an API easier for the next person, and improve tests because the current setup makes everyone afraid to deploy. Your impact should show beyond the pull requests with your name on them. You can work across the stack. A feature might run from a React interaction through GraphQL into a Node service, a schema redesign, a permissions update, and a safe migration for existing customers. Curiosity to follow the problem matters more than equal depth everywhere. You own quality. We have QA. That's not where quality begins. What breaks if this request happens twice? What happens with old data, or when the API fails halfway through? We use Playwright and Jest alongside reviews and monitoring. The goal isn't coverage, it's confidence. You communicate like your decisions will matter later. Six months from now, somebody should understand an important decision without digging through seventeen Slack messages and a deleted Notion comment. That means writing things down when they matter, explaining trade-offs clearly, giving useful code reviews, and surfacing risks before they become incidents. You raise the engineering bar around you. You do not need a management title to have influence. Find the hole in an architecture, unblock someone without taking the keyboard away, disagree without turning every decision into a referendum. As you earn trust, you’ll naturally become the person people bring harder problems to. What you'll do Over your first year: Enterprise integrations: into our customers' systems, data, identity providers, and workflows. This is what turns GlassDollar from software somebody logs into, into infrastructure their organisation operates on. APIs and MCP: public REST APIs and MCP servers for our customers, their engineers, and increasingly their AI agents. The interesting part isn't exposing endpoints, it's designing an external platform we'll still be happy supporting years from now. AI inside real workflows: embeddings, vector search, and LLMs across a large database of startups and corporate innovation data. We're less interested in adding a ✨ button to everything than in finding places where AI removes real work. Workflow automation: triggers, notifications, and automation that replace humans moving information between systems. Core product engineering: React interfaces, APIs, PostgreSQL queries, permissions, migrations, performance work, and the occasional bug whose root cause makes everybody stare silently at their screen. Our stack Frontend: TypeScript, React, Material UI, Apollo Client, Playwright Backend: Node.js, GraphQL, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Jest Infrastructure: AWS, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Sentry Increasingly: LLM APIs, embeddings, vector search, MCP, AI-assisted engineering workflows You don't need experience with every item. Reasoning about systems matters more to us than having memorised our exact stack. Requirements Substantial production experience with TypeScript, React, and Node.js Comfortable reasoning about relational databases, not just the ORM Can independently take a feature from unclear starting point to production Can read unfamiliar code without immediately proposing a rewrite Nice to have: Experience with GraphQL, Prisma, or PostgreSQL at scale Exposure to LLM APIs, embeddings, or vector search Experience owning systems, not just features Don't check every box? Apply anyway. We'd rather have the conversation than lose someone over a bullet point. How we hire How we work We're a small engineering team, so there are fewer places for responsibility to disappear and no chain of five people between you and a decision. We prefer written context over meetings the calendar invented, and working software over elaborate process. Quickly doesn't mean carelessly. Sometimes the fastest route is the simple version today, sometimes it's another day on a foundation twenty future features will sit on. Knowing which situation you're in is part of the job. Expect to ship to production very early. How we hire No seven-stage endurance test. No algorithm trivia disconnected from the work. Intro. You, us, and whether this is the environment you're actually looking for. Technical conversation. We go deep on something difficult you've built: the decisions, the alternatives, what you'd do differently now. Technical assessment. Usually live coding on a realistic problem, sometimes a small proof of concept instead. We care how you think, not whether your solution matches ours. Offer. If there's strong mutual conviction, we move. One last thing Job descriptions have a habit of producing candidates who optimise themselves against bullet points. Please don't. If you're reading this thinking "I can do most of this, but I haven't worked with MCP", apply. Strong fundamentals, meaningful software shipped, and a bias toward ownership are what we're looking for. The rest is learnable. Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Associate Product Owner

Workflow automation inside the platform , so the work that used to take six meetings and a shared spreadsheet runs itself. You will need to understand each of these well enough to write the spec and defend it in the room. This is a doing role rather than a people-management one. Mid-to-senior individual contributor. title: Computational Biologist
description: About us Owkin is an agentic AI company pioneering Biological Artificial Superintelligence to solve problems in biology where human researchers alone have failed. K Pro orchestrates a suite of AI skills and tools to decode complex biology, accelerate research, and dramatically increase productivity. K Pro is built on Owkin’s unrivalled multimodal patient data network, state-of-the-art AI for biology and a decade of experience working with pharmaceutical partners. Position is based in our Paris office or remotely in France, UK or Germany. Please submit your CV in English About the role: As a Computational Biologist at Owkin, you will have a unique opportunity to contribute to the discovery of better treatments through the development and use of agentic AI systems. An integral member of the Biomedical team, you will work alongside world-class experts in AI and biology within a multidisciplinary team dedicated to pioneering discoveries, all while embedded in an organization that develops end-to-end AI systems for clients. Your experience in omics will allow you to contribute to the building of our AI Scientist, an agentic system designed to navigate the complexities of target and drug discovery. In particular, you will: Contribute analyses to projects aiming to discover novel drug targets, biomarkers and disease subtypes through reverse translation based on multi-omics patient or pre-clinical data including: genomic, transcriptomic (spatial, single-cell, bulk), proteomic, and others. analyze biomedical datasets using classical or novel omics methods and machine / deep learning algorithms Conduct literature reviews to stay up-to-date with respect to relevant approaches and datasets Participate in the interpretation of results and help design validation strategies together with cross-functional teams. Collaborate with other members of Owkin’s R&Tech and Biomedical departments with varied backgrounds (computational biologists and chemists, AI scientists, medical imaging experts, medical doctors, biologists, …). Contribute analyses and visualisations to generate scientific internal and external communications and reports. Participate in Owkin’s internal R&D activities, develop new as well as improve existing methodologies, strive to keep Owkin’s Toolbox to the state-of-the-art. About you The successful candidate will have a ‘team-first’ kind of attitude; be curious and detail-attentive; thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment; and be fun to work with. And: Be passionate about the potential for impact when combining AI and healthcare. MSc / PhD in either computational biology, bioinformatics, biology, machine learning, computer science, mathematics or a related field. Experience working with omics data and NGS data processing pipelines. Experience of integrating multi-omics datasets. Experience of working in early-stage drug discovery programs, and with tasks such as target identification, biomarker discovery and patient stratification. Good knowledge about molecular and cellular biology, especially related to cancer and/or other human diseases, to help interpret analyzis results together with our biomedical experts. Familiarity with machine learning concepts and toolkits such as: cross validation, statistical tests, scikit learn, xgboost, etc. Experience using autonomous AI agents and agentic workflows to perform data analyses. Good programming skills in Python. Fluency in written and spoken English. Ways to Stand Out The following experience is not necessarily required, but would be a plus: Single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomic data analysis. Clinical and biomedical imaging data. Hands-on experience with agentic AI systems and their development. History of publications or contributions to top-tier academic journals or conferences. title: Applied AI Engineer, Startups (Codex)

title: Head of Brand (Relocation to Milan)
description: Please note that this opportunity requires relocation to our Milan office. About us Traditional banking has never really given people control over their financial life. Satispay exists to change that: to empower people through finance . That means making financial services easy and accessible for millions of users. We started with payments, then benefits, investing, cards... and we’re not done. Not even close. Same logic every time: find a real problem, solve it properly, then look for the next one. The destination? To build the most loved financial platform in the world. Getting there takes leaders who own outcomes across teams, not just tasks, and set the tone for refusing the “someone else will fix this” culture. If that's how you lead, you'll fit right in. What you'll be doing As our Head of Brand, you'll own the creative and brand strategy end-to-end, bridging the gap between high-level storytelling and measurable business impact, ensuring our mission resonates across every touchpoint. Here's what that looks like in practice: Creative Production - Owning the production of creative assets, ensuring every output meets a consistently high bar of quality, craft, and brand consistency. Brand Activation - Driving both ATL (TV, radio, OOH, print) and BTL/untraditional activations, bringing the brand to life in bold and memorable ways. Social Media & Community - Steering our presence across existing Social media channels and new ones, while building an influencer strategy that extends our reach and relevance. Brand Strategy & Insights - Shaping and safeguarding brand identity, and grounding decisions in research and listening, including surveys with both customers and non-customers. Leadership & Team Rituals - Building and mentoring the team behind these pillars, establishing clear creative rituals (design reviews, sprints, feedback loops) and tools to ensure efficient, high-quality output. Cross-functional Collaboration - Partnering closely with Growth and Product teams to align brand initiatives with acquisition goals, retention targets, and product launches. Performance-Driven Branding - Defining and tracking KPIs for brand awareness and consideration, ensuring that even the most "creative" projects are data-informed and contribute to Satispay's overarching OKRs. You will lead and mentor high-performing teams, collaborate closely with peers with structured communication and transparency, demonstrating a commitment to integrity and ownership. Who we're looking for You'll take on one of the hardest challenges at our scale: defining Satispay's identity globally while ensuring our brand initiatives directly align with acquisition and retention goals — and building the creative team and rituals that stay ahead of it as we grow. We're not looking for a caretaker of an existing setup. We're looking for someone who has built or transformed a function, made hard calls under pressure, and can say "here's the decision, here's why, here's what happened." 10+ years of experience - Proven track record in brand management or creative direction, ideally within fast-growing tech companies or top-tier creative agencies. Strong Technical & Visual Culture - Deep understanding of design systems, rebranding processes, and multi-channel campaign production (from social media to TV/OOH). A "Hands-on" Leader - You love to lead by example. You're not just a "manager of resources" but someone who can get into the details of a layout or a script to ensure excellence. Data-Informed Mindset - Ability to translate brand concepts into business objectives, utilizing KPIs and OKRs to measure impact and iterate quickly. Exceptional Communicator - Fluent in English, with the ability to simplify complex brand visions for internal stakeholders and external audiences alike. We recognise that exceptional leadership comes in many forms. If you believe you have the vision, experience, and drive to help us shape the future of money, we encourage you to apply. We value the unique perspectives and strengths that exceptional leaders bring, even if their experience doesn't align with every listed requirement. Why this is your place This is a unique opportunity to leverage your experience and leadership to make a profound impact on a company poised for significant future growth. We operate on a principle of reciprocity: significant strategic impact are met with meaningful rewards and opportunities. Own outcomes that reach millions . Lead functions where the results show up directly in the experience of 6.5M+ people and the businesses they pay every day. Operate in high-growth. You'll make high-stakes calls without waiting for perfect information, in an environment that changes fast as we launch and scale new products. Significant equity participation. Directly share in Satispay's success through a competitive Stock Option Plan designed to reward leadership and contribution to company growth and raise the bar for collective success. Lead exceptional teams. Build, mentor, and collaborate with high-performing teams in a culture of ownership, collective success, and continuous improvement fueled by feedback. You will learn from the best and lead alongside founders who are hands-on. CareAbout: how we support your impact We move fast, and evolution never stops. It’s a fun ride, but it can be challenging. To make sure our people truly thrive, we’re committed to making their lives easier, both in the office and out in the world. That’s why we created CareAbout: ❤️ Health: private insurance for you and your family, psychological support with Serenis, mental health workshops. 💰 Financial resources: Stock Option Plan, meal vouchers, relocation support if you’re moving countries. ⚙️ Growth and development: professional development programs, internal mobility, language courses with Preply. 🌱 Flexibility: unlimited PTO, hybrid working policy*, flexible working hours. 👨‍👩‍👧 Family: enhanced parental leave, additional leave for child sickness. * We embrace three days per week in-office (Tuesday and Thursday + 1 of your choice), with the option to request extra remote time. Initial salary: Starting from €65,000 gross per annum This baseline is set using objective, gender-neutral criteria for the role's core requirements. However, we do not believe in putting a ceiling on talent. The final compensation package is tailored according to your unique experience and expertise. If your skills go beyond the standard profile, apply anyway so we can discuss a package that reflects your true value. title: Director, People Operations & Total Rewards
description: 🌀 The Company Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action. Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action. At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative. As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future. 🎯 The Role We’re looking for a hands-on, globally experienced People leader and builder to help take Filigran’s People organization through its next stage of scale. Reporting to the Chief People Officer, you’ll lead our global People Operations, Payroll and Total Rewards capabilities across Europe, North America and APJ. With ~300 employees across 18 countries, the challenge is not simply to build more People infrastructure — it’s to build smarter infrastructure . You’ll help create a scalable, technology- and AI-first People operating model that combines strong regional execution with effective systems, automation, and agentic AI. This is a builder and player-coach role . You’ll be expected to challenge how work gets done, simplify before adding complexity, automate before adding headcount, and build the People capabilities needed to support Filigran’s next stage of growth. 💼 Your Responsibilities Lead and scale global People Operations , continuously building and improving the operating model, team and infrastructure required to support Filigran’s next stage of growth across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond. Lead and develop our regional People Ops and Payroll teams , creating clear accountability, strong regional expertise and consistent global execution, with a strong focus on employee lifecycle experience . Build and continuously optimize an AI-first People operating model through process automation that simplifies and systemizes repeatable work; agentic AI that autonomously handles complex, low-risk, multi-step workflows requiring reasoning, decisions and escalation; and an integrated People technology ecosystem that connects systems, workflows and data into scalable infrastructure. Own global payroll operations , working with internal specialists and external providers to ensure accuracy, strong controls and timely multi-country execution. Own global Total Rewards operations , including compensation cycles, benchmarking, benefits, equity reporting and vendor management, in partnership with the CPO on strategy. Oversee global employment compliance and mobility , including regional compliance, immigration, EORs and entity-related People requirements, leveraging local experts and counsel where appropriate. Use People data and insights to proactively identify organizational trends, risks and opportunities , translating them into practical actions for leaders and the wider People team. Support organizational design and workforce planning , bringing data, organizational insight and implementation capability to CPO-led decisions. Support managers on routine performance, employee relations, workforce matters and organizational change. Remain hands-on and execution-oriented , moving fluidly between team leadership, systems and agent design, process improvement and complex operational problem-solving. 🤝 Who You’ll Work With Chief People Officer — partnering closely on People priorities, Total Rewards strategy and the evolution of our global People operating model. People Operations, Payroll teams — leading and developing these capabilities globally. Talent Acquisition, Learning & Development and Employee Experience — partnering across the broader People organization. People Managers, Finance, Legal, and IT — partnering on employee matters, payroll, rewards, compliance, systems and global operations. External partners and advisors — including EORs, payroll and benefits providers, employment counsel and mobility partners. 🧬 Profile We’re Looking For 10+ years of progressive HR / People experience , with leadership across People Operations and Total Rewards . Proven experience helping scale a global B2B SaaS, cybersecurity or enterprise technology company from approximately 300+ employees through significant growth . Strong global experience across Europe, North America and APJ , including multiple entities, EORs and complex European employment environments. Significant experience across People Operations, payroll, Total Rewards, Systems, and Compliance , with a track record of building infrastructure for scale . Highly technology- and AI-oriented , with demonstrated experience using automation, AI agents and agentic workflows to redesign work and increase People team capacity. Strong systems, data and commercial mindset , able to connect People infrastructure, insights and decisions to business priorities. Strong people leader who builds high-performing teams through trust, clarity, development and accountability. High EQ and strong influencing skills — collaborative, low-ego and direct, with the ability to build credibility, challenge constructively and navigate complex dynamics. Hands-on, player-coach mentality , equally comfortable partnering with leaders and directly solving operational, systems and organizational problems in a fast-growing, global, remote-first environment. Fluent in English and French; additional languages are a plus. 🌱 Why Join Filigran? More than just a job. We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company , and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation . You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem. ⭐ Be part of something bigger We believe we do work that matters. Our open-source approach means that work extends beyond Filigran. You’re contributing to technology and ideas that strengthen a global community of defenders and help make cybersecurity more open and collaborative. 💻 Work at the edge of what’s next We bring together cybersecurity, open source and AI — giving you the opportunity to work with emerging technologies, experiment with new ways of working, and contribute to how they are applied in practice. 🌍 Global opportunity without borders Be part of a fast-growing, truly international team — collaborating across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond, with the flexibility of a remote-first environment. As we grow, you’ll have opportunities to expand your scope, take ownership, learn quickly and grow with us. 🧭 A culture grounded in CORE Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity define how we work together — with openness, ownership, collaboration and respect. These are the principles that guide how we make decisions, treat people and grow together, especially when no one’s watching. 💰 What you can expect Competitive compensation + equity — everyone shares in our success Remote-first flexibility — work from wherever you’re based, with flexibility built into how we operate 25 days PTO baseline — real time to disconnect, recharge and enjoy life outside work Volunteer days — paid time to contribute to causes that matter to you Set up for success — choose the equipment that works for you, with additional support for your remote work and development needs as our programs evolve Two annual in-person get-togethers — one global company get-together and one team get-together, creating dedicated time to connect, collaborate and strengthen our culture beyond the screen 🌍 Equal Employment Opportunity We enable cybersecurity through inclusion — from code to culture. At Filigran, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe the diversity of our people makes our products and our team stronger. We welcome talent of every background, identity and lived experience, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability or veteran status. What matters here is what you bring, not what you look like, where you’re from or how you identify. 🚀 Ready to Join Us? Apply now and help us build the future of the cybersecurity ecosystem, together. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Engineering Manager
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><div id="message-list_1790155756.049469"> <div> <div> <div> <div> <div> <div> <div> <div> <div> <div> <div><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Engineering Manager, Production Engineering - Observability</strong></span></div> <div> </div> <div><strong>An overview of this role</strong><br>You'll lead the globally distributed Observability team. The team builds and operates the metrics, logging, alerting, and capacity planning platforms that GitLab engineers use to understand <a href="http://GitLab.com" target="_blank">GitLab.com</a> and GitLab Dedicated. You'll help determine how the team collects, stores, queries, and acts on telemetry, balancing reliable signals with scale and cost.<br>In your first year, you'll guide improvements to Prometheus-based metrics pipelines, log ingestion and retention, alerting driven by service-level objectives (SLOs), and capacity forecasting. You'll work with Site Reliability Engineering, Product Engineering, and other Infrastructure Platforms teams to make it easier for engineers to observe the services they own. You'll also take part in incident response and help keep the team's on-call work sustainable.<br><strong>What you’ll do</strong></div> <ul> <li>Lead, hire, onboard, and develop a distributed engineering team working asynchronously.</li> <li>Set priorities with Site Reliability Engineering, Product Engineering, and GitLab Dedicated teams, and help the team deliver observability services iteratively.</li> <li>Own the reliability, scalability, and cost of the team's metrics, logging, alerting, and capacity planning platforms.</li> <li>Reduce noisy or missing alerts and telemetry gaps, and use SLOs, error budgets, and self-service instrumentation to help engineers maintain the health of their services.</li> <li>Guide technical decisions about time-series storage, high-cardinality metrics, log pipelines, and distributed tracing.</li> <li>Participate in the Incident Manager On Call (IMOC) rotation, coordinating the response to high-severity incidents affecting <a href="http://GitLab.com" target="_blank">GitLab.com</a>.</li> <li>Keep the team's on-call rotation sustainable through coverage across time zones, useful runbooks, better alerts, and follow-through on post-incident actions.</li> <li>Use AI tools and agents to support engineering workflows and incident triage, reviewing their output while engineers retain responsibility for decisions.</li> </ul> <div><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></div> <ul> <li>Experience leading an observability, platform engineering, or site reliability engineering team operating at scale, including supporting people in a distributed, asynchronous environment.</li> <li>Technical knowledge of metrics systems such as Prometheus and long-term storage, logging platforms such as Elasticsearch or cloud-native services, and alerting design.</li> <li>Experience using SLOs, error budgets, and capacity forecasts to make reliability and investment decisions.</li> <li>Experience operating a large software-as-a-service platform and investigating production issues such as telemetry gaps, ingestion limits, or noisy and missing alerts.</li> <li>Experience participating in and improving production on-call rotations, including incident coordination and balancing operational load with project work.</li> <li>The ability to explain technical tradeoffs to engineering partners and other stakeholders.</li> <li>Experience using AI tools or agents in engineering or management work; you can describe how you would apply them to operational problems such as incident triage.</li> </ul> <div>We welcome different paths into this role, whether through practical experience, formal study, or transferable skills. If the work interests you, please apply even if you don't meet every qualification.</div> <div> </div> <div><strong>About the team</strong><br>We're part of Production Engineering within Infrastructure Platforms and work asynchronously across regions. Our tools include Tamland, the capacity forecasting tool. We bring lessons from operating GitLab's production systems back into the platforms we build.</div> <div> </div> <div> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. Our </span><strong><span data-contrast="none">AI solutions</span></strong><span data-contrast="auto"> enhance efficiency, spark creativity, and drive insightful decision-making, empowering our teams to produce innovative and impactful results.</span> </p></div><h3>Solution Design Architect (AI / Transformation / Creative Operations)</h3> <p><span data-ccp-props="{"335559739":240}"><strong>Language requirement:</strong> <span style="text-decoration: underline;">fluency in German or Spanish</span></span></p> <p><span data-ccp-props="{"335559739":240}"><strong><span data-contrast="auto">Location: </span></strong><span data-contrast="auto">Germany (primarily remote) and regular business travel across EMEA</span></span></p> <p><span data-ccp-props="{"335559739":240}"><strong>Employment: </strong>18-month FTC with view to extend</span></p> <p> </p> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">About the role:</span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{"335559739":240}"> </span></p> <p>We’re hiring a Solution Design Architect to help us win and shape new business. You’ll sit in the room with senior client stakeholders, including CMOs, and turn their challenges into operating models, workflows and commercial models (team shapes, asset rates, outcome-based structures) that we can deliver. You’ll bring the commercial judgement to validate the numbers, the process thinking to design better ways of working, and the technical and channel knowledge to lead the conversation when specialists aren’t there. Quick on your feet and calm under pressure, you’ll be supported by our Commercial and Implementation teams.</p> <h4> </h4> <h4>Key Responsibilities:</h4> <h4>New Business and Client Engagement</h4> <ul> <li>Lead the operational and solution design element of new client pitches, presenting with credibility and confidence to senior client stakeholders, including CMOs and marketing leadership.</li> <li>Formulate solutions in real time during pitches, workshops and challenging client discussions, staying composed and commercially sharp.</li> <li>Own the conversation on technology and data when technical specialists aren’t present, and know when and how to bring them in.</li> <li>Ensure a smooth handover from pitch to implementation, so what we sell is what we deliver.</li> </ul> <h4>Requirement Gathering and Analysis</h4> <ul> <li>Work with stakeholders to gather, document and analyse business requirements for new client accounts.</li> <li>Ask the right questions to define accurate scope, cost and risk.</li> <li>Translate client business needs into workflows for client and technology teams.</li> </ul> <h4>Operating Model and Solution Design</h4> <ul> <li>Define and articulate operating model principles (roles, governance, ways of working, handoffs) that align to client goals and our delivery capability.</li> <li>Evaluate existing client and internal processes, identify new ways of working, and recommend improvements for efficiency, cost reduction and better outcomes.</li> <li>Design solutions across advertising and marketing channels, drawing on a strong understanding of how media, data, creative and technology fit together.</li> <li>Collaborate with technology and business teams to ensure solutions align with our strategy and are technically feasible.</li> </ul> <h4>Commercial Modelling</h4> <ul> <li>Build, test and validate commercial models that deliver the designed workflow, including team shapes, asset-based rate models and outcome-based models.</li> <li>Work with Commercial and Finance to pressure-test assumptions, margins and risk before models go to clients.</li> <li>Balance client value with commercial viability, and explain the reasoning clearly to both internal and client audiences.</li> </ul> <h4>Stakeholder Communication</h4> <ul> <li>Act as the bridge between clients, commercial, technology and delivery teams, ensuring shared understanding and alignment.</li> <li>Translate complex technical and commercial concepts into clear, compelling narratives for non-technical, senior audiences.</li> </ul> <h4>Data, Measurement and Reporting</h4> <ul> <li>Analyse data to support decision-making, and define measurement frameworks for new clients.</li> <li>Create reports and presentations that convey findings and recommendations with clarity and impact.</li> </ul> <h4> </h4> <h4>About You:</h4> <h4>Essential</h4> <ul> <li>10-15 years’ experience in solution design, consulting, strategy, operations or a similar role within advertising, marketing, media or marketing technology.</li> <li>A confident, articulate communicator with a track record of presenting to and influencing C-suite and senior marketing stakeholders (CMOs or equivalent).</li> <li>Commercial acumen, with hands-on experience building and validating pricing or commercial models (e.g. resourcing/team-shape models, rate cards, outcome-based or performance-linked structures).</li> <li>A process-driven mindset, able to map, challenge and redesign ways of working and articulate clear operating model principles.</li> <li>Strong working knowledge of advertising and marketing channels (e.g. paid media, social, programmatic, search, CRM, creative production) and how they connect to data and technology.</li> <li>Enough technical fluency in martech, adtech, data and platforms to hold credible conversations with clients and lead when technical specialists aren’t in the room.</li> <li>Quick-thinking and resilient, comfortable formulating answers and options in high-pressure or contentious situations while maintaining client confidence.</li> <li>Strong analytical skills, with the ability to turn data into insight and recommendations.</li> <li>Willingness and flexibility to travel regularly for client pitches, mostly across Europe and occasionally further afield.</li> </ul> <h4>Desirable</h4> <ul> <li>Experience contributing to new business wins, RFPs and pitch processes.</li> <li>Experience in an agency, consultancy or in-house marketing transformation environment.</li> <li>Experience with global or multi-market clients and remote, cross-functional teams.</li> </ul> <h4> </h4> <h4>What Success Looks Like:</h4> <ul> <li>Contribute directly to new business wins and improve pitch win rates.</li> title: Consultant
description: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. Location This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with occasional visits to customers across the DACH region. As team collaboration is of great importance to us, we highly encourage team members to join us in Zurich at least once a month. These visits are financially supported by BLP. About the role For a process to run autonomously, four things have to line up: the technology, the process itself, the data behind it, and the people who work with it. That alignment does not happen at go-live. It happens in the months after, and that is where this role sits. Our customers go live with a working solution. What they do not have on day one is an organisation that operates in an AI-native way. Processes were designed around people checking things. Data was maintained well enough for humans to interpret. Teams know the old workarounds better than the new system. Your job is to lead that transition, from a process that is automated in parts to a process that genuinely runs on its own. That means working across every level of the customer's organisation. With operational teams you build understanding and find where automation is actually blocked. With department leads you challenge the process rules that make full automation impossible, and drive the decisions that change them. And you use the right lever for each blocker, because they are all different: some are a data clean-up you coordinate with the customer, some are a training and adoption gap, some need a custom agent, and some are structural and belong with our engineering teams. You do not do this alone. You enable the customer's core team to solve their own issues, you work with our Customer Success Engineers on the technical side, and you use the Customer Success Manager to get decisions made where you need commercial weight. For our smaller customers, where there is no Customer Success Manager, you are the escalation point yourself. You own customer health. Your sharpest measure of it is the automation rate. What you'll do Own customer health across your portfolio, measured first and foremost by automation rates. Lead the transition to AI-native ways of working: identify what blocks automation, and pick the right way to solve each blocker. Work with operational teams on enablement and adoption, so people work efficiently with blp rather than around it. Challenge process rules that prevent automation, and drive improvements with the department leads who can decide. Coordinate data clean-up with the customer where master data quality is capping what automation can reach. Enable the customer's core team to resolve issues themselves, and reduce what has to come to us at all. Identify where a custom agent solves the problem, and where the issue is structural and belongs with our engineering teams. Collaborate with Customer Success Engineers on technical topics, and with the Customer Success Manager to get decisions made. For customers without a Customer Success Manager, act as the escalation point for SLA breaches and own continuity of operations. Direct the AI Automation Specialists working on your accounts. What we're really looking for The following key attributes ensure success in this role: Process Excellence – You understand core business processes deeply, P2P and O2C, and you can see why a process is shaped the way it is and what it could look like instead. Client Hands – You bring customers with you. You are strict on the things that matter and flexible on the things that do not, you understand the context people are working in, and you have more than one way of convincing them. Ownership & Autonomy – You take a customer from live to high automation without being told the steps. Comfort in the Data – You go into the numbers yourself to find where automation is leaking. Problem Solving & Critical Thinking – You separate a configuration symptom from a process cause, and pick the right lever for each. What you'll bring Master's degree in Business, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. 3+ years of experience in consulting, process improvement, shared services, or ERP process ownership. Deep working knowledge of at least one core business process end to end, purchase-to-pay or order-to-cash. This is a prerequisite, not a nice to have. Demonstrable experience changing how a finance, procurement or supply chain team actually works, not only advising on it. Strong analytical skills. You are comfortable working with process and transaction data directly. Confident facilitating workshops with operational teams and presenting to their leadership. Fluent in German and English, spoken and written. Bonus points for experience with ERP systems, accounts payable or order management processes, or AI-driven SaaS. What you'll get High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path. Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises. Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily. Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression. Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option programme. Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators. Technology exposure – be at the forefront of emerging technologies and enjoy continuous learning opportunities. Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites. Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact. Learn more about blp and our values at https://blp.digital/company/careers . Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Customer Success Engineer
description: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. Location This is a full-time position based at our HQ in Munich or Cologne. About the role You solve the hard technical problems on live systems. Once a customer is running on blp, their processes are business critical. Invoices post or they do not. Orders flow or they sit. Our support organisation resolves most of what comes in, and a lot of it is genuinely well handled by people early in their career. What is left is yours: the cases where the cause is not obvious, where it crosses systems, data and process logic at once, where the same symptom has three possible explanations and only one of them is right. That is the job. Not a queue, and not the easy half of one. Everything difficult that comes out of the run phase lands with you. Two things sit alongside the case work, and they are what make this a senior job rather than a harder version of a junior one. Stabilising accounts When an account's health goes bad, you go in and stabilise it. Not as a permanent assignment, but as a small, highly skilled squad that takes a customer whose numbers or whose confidence have slipped, works out what is actually wrong across the whole picture, fixes it, and hands back a customer who is running properly again. It is the most concentrated version of this work there is. Taking effort out permanently Anything that keeps arriving in the queue is a signal, and the answer is usually not more people answering it. It might be better self-service for customers, a customer-facing assistant that resolves the routine questions before they reach us, better diagnostics, or a change in how something is configured at deployment so the problem never occurs. You are expected to find those, make the case, and drive them through. That is how a support organisation scales without scaling headcount one for one, and it is value the customer feels directly. You work across the boundary between what our platform does, what the customer's ERP does, and what their data actually looks like. You are the one who can read a failing case end to end and say what really happened, and then say credibly whether the fix is configuration, data, process, or a genuine product issue. When it is a product issue, you are the counterpart to our engineering and product teams: you bring the evidence, and because you have seen the same structural problem across several customers, your case is the one that moves the roadmap. You are also how this function gets better rather than just bigger. The diagnostic tooling, the patterns, the documentation that lets a first-year person resolve what used to take a senior one: that is yours to build. And the interns and specialists coming through the team learn this craft from you. You do not deliver integrations and you do not run go-lives. Our integrations engineers and technical project managers own that. You own what happens once it is live and it is challenging. What you'll do Own the technically difficult cases from our live customer base, end to end, to a verified root cause. Diagnose across boundaries: platform behaviour, ERP behaviour, master data and process logic. Decide what the real fix is, and make it: configuration, data, process, or a case for engineering. Go into accounts with a deteriorating health score, diagnose across the whole picture, stabilise them and hand them back running properly. Drive strategic initiatives that permanently reduce effort and improve the customer experience, from better diagnostics to customer-facing self-service and assistants. Act as the counterpart to Product and Engineering, with evidence strong enough to change priorities. Recognise structural problems across customers and push for them to be solved once. Build the diagnostic tooling, patterns and documentation that raise what the rest of the team can resolve alone. Mentor interns and earlier-career colleagues, and raise the technical bar of the function. Support Consultants and Customer Success Managers on the technical substance of customer escalations. What we're really looking for The following key attributes ensure success in this role: Root Cause, Not Symptom – You are not finished when it stops happening. You are finished when you know why. Cross-Boundary Reasoning – You hold platform, ERP, data and process in your head at once and find where the truth is. Credible Both Ways – You explain the same problem to an engineer and to a CFO, and both of them believe you. Leverage – Your instinct is to remove the next hundred cases, not only to close this one. You would rather build the thing that makes a problem stop arriving. Calm Under Escalation – When a business-critical process is stopped, you get more precise rather than faster. Stabilizer Under Pressure : An unhappy client is not a fire to put out. It is a relationship to rebuild. You bring the temperature down, put structure back into the account, and align next steps so trust returns, not just silence What you'll bring Master's degree in a STEM field: computer science, engineering, information systems, mathematics, physics or similar. Strong candidates from a related field are welcome to make their case. 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role: application support at depth, technical consulting, solution engineering, integration engineering or equivalent. Demonstrable debugging ability across systems, not only within one. APIs, data mapping, interfaces, logs. Comfortable with data. SQL or equivalent, and the instinct to check rather than assume. German and English, both fluent. This is a hard requirement. Our customers work in German every day and our internal work runs in English. Nice to have: ERP experience with SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or similar, scripting in any language, or exposure to workflow automation and process mining. What you'll get The hard problems, not the queue. Influence on the product, with a direct line to Engineering and Product. Room to shape the function, since the practice is still being built. Real growth – the path from here leads into Consulting, technical leadership within Customer Success, or Product. Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option programme. Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators. Visits & offsites – including collaborative team offsites. Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact. Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers . Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

Location This is a six-month internship based in Munich or Cologne. This is an in-person role. You learn this job by sitting next to people who already do it, and that does not work remotely. About the role Think of this role as the modern Sherlock Holmes — new puzzles to solve and new people to work with, every single day. This role sits exactly at the intersection of technology and business, and that is not a figure of speech. On one side you are in the system, in the data, working out what actually happened. That is where your work starts, and it is also where you become the face of blp for that customer. What reaches them is you: your answer, your explanation, your judgement about what to do next. You will not be reading from a script and escalating. You investigate what the system did, what the data says and what the customer's process actually requires. You have the access and the authority to change configuration when that is the answer. And when it is not, you know who to bring in and what to give them. The role grows with you. You start on cases where the pattern is known and someone is close by. As your expertise builds you take the harder ones, and your exposure to customers grows with it: from written answers, to calls, to being in the room when a customer wants their most pressing problem solved now. This goes well beyond tickets. We are a fast-moving organisation and a lot of what needs to exist does not exist yet. You will take on and drive initiatives that make the whole operation scale: a recurring problem that should be solved once rather than fifty times, a piece of tooling that does not exist, a way of working that has outgrown itself. Interns here have shipped things that the team still uses. How we think about ownership You will be given real work with real consequences, early, because that is the only way anyone learns this job properly. The other half of that is judgement: explore and decide for yourself where you can, and pull someone in when something critical is on the line. The role is highly cross-functional: you'll bridge our software and hardware capabilities with the rigorous requirements of the four German Transmission System Operators (TSOs) and 900+ Distribution System Operators (DSOs). The detailed Gateway (Kraken’s IoT Edge Hardware&Software) configuration and protocol engineering is owned by our UK-based team, whom you will feed with regional knowledge and design input, and who will support you on the technical aspects of how Kraken integrations work. This can cover both new projects and retrofits. Regional Technical Expertise: Be the regional authority who feeds and supports the UK team with knowledge of German hardware requirements, industrial protocols, connectivity, cyber-security expectations, and TSO/DSO and ancillary-service requirements. Help evaluate hardware and connectivity solutions for regional fit. Stakeholder Liaison: Act as the technical point of contact for TSOs, DSOs, customers, and internal commercial teams to resolve connection, onboarding, or operational issues. Hardware & On-site Support (occasional): Hardware is deployed remotely in most cases via O&Ms and third parties. However, occasional regional support and hands-on intervention may be required before or after a deployment, including some hardware handling and on-site engineering. You’ll ideally be based close to Kraken’s Berlin office and the role requires the ability to travel when needed, though this is kept to a minimum. 🧠 What you'll bring to the party Language: Native or professional fluency in German and English , essential for technical documentation and TSO/regulator communication. Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, or a related field ( or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration). Integration & connectivity: Proven experience establishing industrial communication and connectivity between field equipment and external systems (telemetry and/or control). Power-plant systems: Working understanding of power-plant control systems and instrumentation, including metering. German market knowledge: TSO/DSO hierarchy and the connection/integration process. Ancillary services (FCR, aFRR, mFRR) prequalification and technical requirements. Redispatch 3.0 regulatory framework. Customer-facing delivery: Ability to produce technical integration approaches and communicate them to customers, regulators, and internal teams. Travel: Occasional travel may be required. A drive to get things done in a collaborative, agile environment , comfortable navigating the complexity of a multi-TSO, decentralised grid, and comfortable being the regional face of a technical function whose deep build sits with a partner team in the UK. ⭐️ Bonus points Knowledge of industrial communication protocols: IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25 (wind), OPC-UA, Modbus , or similar IEC protocols. Understanding of IT/OT security in the energy sector ( NIS2, EnWG/KRITIS awareness ; IEC 62443 a plus). Familiarity with CLI tools for configuring, diagnosing, and maintaining hardware or network connections in remote, Linux-based environments. Familiarity with software languages, version-controlled configuration, and general tooling. Exposure to the wider European balancing markets / ENTSO-E frameworks beyond Germany. About the role We’re looking for a Senior or Staff Product Engineer to help build the next generation of Passionfroot. You’ll work across the full stack on both our core platform and Zest, our AI Campaign Manager for creator marketing. That could mean designing a new workflow for managing creator campaigns, making collaboration data feel instant, or turning models, search, and product context into a reliable AI experience that customers can trust. We don’t separate “AI engineering” from “product engineering.” AI is becoming part of how the product works, but great product fundamentals still matter: understanding the user, shaping the problem, choosing the right architecture, building a thoughtful experience, and operating it reliably in production. You’ll work closely with the founders, design, and customers to take important problems from early exploration to shipped product. We’re a team of six engineers, and staying small is deliberate. It means you can have an idea on Monday and have customers using it by Thursday—without layers of sprint ceremonies or alignment meetings in between. The flip side is real ownership: you need to exercise strong judgment, communicate your decisions, and think through their consequences rather than wait for someone else to catch them. 📍This role is based in our Berlin or São Paulo offices with a hybrid work model. What you’ll do Own meaningful product areas from problem definition through architecture, implementation, launch, and iteration. Build customer-facing features across our marketplace, campaign management, collaboration, payments, analytics, and creator workflows. Help make Zest an indispensable part of how modern companies run creator-led growth. Turn foundation models into structured, reliable product experiences—not just impressive prototypes. Work on intelligent workflows involving agents, tools, retrieval, search, recommendations, and generated interfaces. Develop the evaluations, observability, and feedback loops needed to understand whether AI features are genuinely useful. Work closely with design to create experiences that are fast, intuitive, and polished. Talk directly with customers and translate ambiguous needs into simple product decisions. Make pragmatic architectural choices that balance speed, quality, maintainability, and performance. Improve the systems and engineering practices that help a small team ship reliably at high velocity. At Staff level, provide technical direction across projects, raise the engineering bar, and help other engineers make better decisions. What we’re looking for Significant experience building and shipping high-quality, customer-facing software. 5+ years is a useful guide, but the scope and quality of your work matter more than the number. Strong TypeScript and React fundamentals, with experience working across the full stack. A track record of independently driving complex features or products from an ambiguous starting point to measurable customer impact. When you encounter a blocker, you investigate, communicate, and find another path forward without waiting to be managed. Strong product and technical judgment. You care about what should be built, how it should feel, and whether it actually solves the problem. You can distinguish between problems that need a sophisticated system and problems that need a simple, well-executed solution. Experience building with LLMs or other applied AI systems in production. We release weekly. Native releases can't be rolled back once they're out, so we care about getting each one right: tests, careful review, and watching what happens after release. Who we are looking for Several years building and releasing iOS apps used at scale Deep experience with Swift, app architecture and refactoring code that's already live Testing and coding habits for stable app releases You make the developers around you better, through review, pairing and clear explanation You can explain a technical trade-off to product and design in plain terms If you meet most of these but not all, we'd still like to hear from you. We'll help you grow into the rest. Nice to have SwiftUI, reactive programming and GraphQL A/B testing, phased rollouts and data tracking Monitoring tools such as Datadog Android or cross-platform experience An interest in electronic music and the scenes RA serves What we offer you Generous annual leave policies aimed at promoting work-life balance. Matched pension, or 401k for US staff. Comprehensive staff wellbeing initiatives, featuring regular activities and workplace programmes to support mental and physical health. This includes discounted ClassPass memberships and custom-fitted earplugs. Company-led social events, team lunches, and discounts on merch. Paid annual volunteering allowance, encouraging contributions to community projects and charities you care about. A transparent internal company culture committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion (see: https://ra.co/about/diversity ). Active involvement in community projects within the electronic music community (see: https://ra.co/about/community ). Craft first, and then a genuine stake in this music rather than just a job in it. title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer / SRE – Kubernetes & Hybrid Cloud (m/f/d)
description: Introduction At a glance Location & work model : Berlin, hybrid Tech stack: Kubernetes on our own servers, Harvester ( KubeVirt ), Argo CD/Flux, Prometheus/Grafana, Longhorn/Ceph Team: A growing SRE team – you report to our CTPO for now and to the Team Lead SRE we're hiring next; two system administrators in Pforzheim run the physical hardware Process: Intro call · take-home task (~2h) · 90-min tech interview with our developers · leadership conversation · meet the team Languages: Fluent English required; German is a plus, not a must Why this role is special Most SRE jobs today mean clicking around a managed cloud console. This one doesn't. We run our own hardware in Frankfurt and are building a modern private cloud platform on Kubernetes and Harvester – on-prem by default, with elastic burst into the public cloud and the option to go cloud-only later. You won't inherit a finished SRE practice: you'll help define it, side by side with our Berlin development teams – and you won't do it alone, a Team Lead SRE hire is coming next. SRE here is an enabling discipline: you build what our developers need to ship reliably, while two system administrators in Pforzheim run the physical hardware. And the impact is direct – our product discovery technology powers more than 2,000 European online shops (Intersport, SPAR, Douglas and more), handling billions of shopper queries a year. When product discovery is slow or down, our customers lose revenue in real time. Your first 90 days You get to know both products, join the on-call rotation with a buddy, and own your first reliability topic – SLOs for one product, alerting that actually helps at 3 a.m., or automating away a piece of toil. By day 90 you've shipped visible improvements and know where you want to take the platform next. Your mission Define and own SLOs, SLIs and error budgets; drive data-informed reliability decisions Lead incident response end-to-end: fast detection, clear communication, blameless postmortems – and reduce whole classes of incidents structurally, not case by case Eliminate toil through automation and GitOps; evolve our observability (metrics, logs, traces, alerting, runbooks) across two different stacks Help build our custom Kubernetes operator (CRDs) that makes stateful search clusters declarative, self-healing and safely upgradable – and roll out the auto-scaling (HPA/VPA, KEDA, cluster auto scaler) today's architecture makes hard Plan capacity, performance and cost across on-premises and cloud – including the large-catalogue and peak-season loads our merchants care about – and use AI tools wherever they measurably speed up diagnosis and operations Your profile Must-haves: Kubernetes in production – built, not just used : you've set up and maintained clusters on your own servers (e.g. kubeadm , RKE2, k3s) and know cluster lifecycle and upgrades – managed-only experience isn't enough for this role Lived SRE practice : SLOs, error budgets, incident management, on-call Hands-on experience with GitOps or comparable infrastructure/deployment automation – experience with Argo CD or Flux is a strong plus Solid observability skills – metrics, logs, traces, alerting that people trust A strong automation instinct – you'd rather fix a problem's cause than repeat its workaround A collaborative, enabling mindset – you see SRE as a service to our developers: you ask what they need, discuss trade-offs openly, and don't fall in love with your own solution Nice-to-haves (genuinely optional – we'll teach you the rest): Harvester, KubeVirt , vSphere/ ESXi , OpenStack or similar virtualization/HCI platforms Container storage (Longhorn, Ceph) and datacenter networking (load balancing, ingress, VLAN) Auto-scaling (HPA, VPA, KEDA, cluster auto scaler ) and capacity/cost planning Experience building Kubernetes operators/CRDs German language skills Certifications (CKA, CKS) are welcome but no substitute for hands-on experience – in the tech interview we'll ask about what you've actually built and operated. You don't tick every box – or your title was never “SRE”? Apply anyway. If you've owned production systems, handled incidents and worked deeply with Kubernetes, we want to hear from you – production experience and engineering mindset matter more to us than titles or buzzwords. THE JOY OF WORKING WITH US Impact from day one: Your work directly influences the revenue of leading eCommerce brands across Europe. Modern tech stack: Kubernetes, Harvester, GitOps, auto-scaling, and an exciting path toward the cloud – with room to build things right. AI-first mindset: We use AI as a real part of our daily work, not as a buzzword. Ownership & growth: Clear responsibility, short decision paths, and the opportunity to actively shape your role. Flexible work: Hybrid work model three office days per week with a focus on outcomes. Strong team: Experienced engineers, an open feedback culture, and an environment where reliability is treated as a real engineering discipline. title: Senior Product Manager, Wealth & AI (f/m/d)
description: What we do At getquin, we're on a mission to empower everyone to build wealth. Founded in 2020, we started with a simple idea: help people see their entire financial life in one place, so they can make more informed decisions. Today, getquin has grown into one of the largest wealth platforms globally, already helping over half a million users manage and grow their wealth. Our platform combines analytics, tools and community to make wealth-building accessible for everyone, not just the experts. After launching in Germany, we've started expanding across Europe, with a focus on growing our user base, building valuable new features and helping even more people take control of their financial future. If you're excited to help shape the future of personal wealth management, join us. We're just getting started. What you'll be doing You've built products for investors. You know what a TER actually does to a long-run return, why a user with four brokers has no visbility what they really own, and how differently people behave when the number on screen is their pension rather than their pocket money. You've probably also hit the ceiling of what a chart can tell someone. Better tables, more filters, another allocation donut. The data was always there; the answer never quite arrived. We have something nobody else has: a complete, cross-institution picture of a person's wealth. Investments, cash, liabilities and insurance contracts, in one place, for over half a million users. Your work is turning that into features and insights people understand and act on, and the interesting tools for doing that now include AI. We're looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager to own that area. You'll work directly with the founders and the product team, alongside engineering and our financial advisory teams. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports, and you'll mentor less experienced product managers on the team. Strong plus if you have: PSD2, open banking or account aggregation experience Insurance or brokerage product exposure, which matters as we move into advisory Recommendation systems or personalisation at scale Subscription and paywall experimentation Experience mentoring or coaching other product managers Your own portfolio, and opinions about it If you meet most of this and not all of it, apply. We'd rather tell you now than after four conversations. What the first six months look like Month 1: you know the data model, the aggregation layer and its technology behind it. What our analytics do and don't cover, and understand how AI is already being used and where it. You've written down the three things you think are most wrong with the product today Months 2 to 3: a written, agreed area strategy with a prioritised roadmap, a primary metric with a baseline, and, clear metrics that you will be monitoring and optimizing along the way Months 3 to 4: the first thing you scoped is live to a user segment, with a read on the primary metric, and with quality measurement behind it if it involves generated output Months 5 to 6: two or three shipped iterations with measured results, including the ones that didn't work, a quality bar the team applies without you in the room, and at least one junior product manager who's visibly better at their job because of you You won't be measured on shipping volume. You'll be measured on whether your area got measurably more useful and more trustworthy. Why join getquin? Why join getquin? We're a fast-growing B2C fintech, and here, your work has real impact. From day one, you'll take ownership of your domain, ship features end-to-end, and help shape the direction of a product used across Europe.
